newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Cocoa seen edging up, may clear 1,020 st.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Cocoa seen edging up, may clear 1,020 st.

text.p: MAY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
London cocoa futures could rise to clear the immediate 1,020 stg hurdle basis May but further gains may be difficult, analysts said on Tuesday.
Traders called the market to open five stg higher in sympathy with New York's advance on Monday.
New York's May closed up $6 at $1,418 a tonne on late local short-covering. But London's gains were slim.
Elli Gifford, an independent technical analyst, said London's May could be cushioned at around 1,000 stg, a level which is likely to hold after Monday's firm close.
"The downside is reasonably limited for the time being," she said.
On the upside, the market could take out the initial 1,020 stg resistance. But beyond that, the ride could be bumpy.
"The resistance is getting difficult as it gets to the 1,030 area," Gifford said. "There are quite a lot of resistance stretching from there all the way up to 1,050 area."
The 14-day relative strength indicator of overbought and oversold conditions was a neutral 54 percent.

Among fundamental news, producer associations in Brazil's key cocoa area of Bahia were divided on the size of the region's upcoming midcrop, with estimates ranging between 800,000 and 1.1 million 60-kg bags.

According to director of the Brazilian Cocoa Producers' Association, the midcrop could drop to as low as 800,000 bags because of dry weather earlier this year and the spread of the lethal witch's broom disease.
"The range is between 800,000 bags and 900,000 bags...But it should be nearer to 800,000 bags," said Jose Mendes.

But the president of the National Cocoa Producers' Council (CNPC) believes the recent rains have helped recuperate some previous losses with the result he is now expecting a crop of between 900,000 to 1.1 million bags.
"Without doubt, the outlook is more optimistic," said Wallace Setenta.
